Long Stroke Thrusters
Seismic Test Systems
-
Unholtz-Dickie Corporation
Seismic Test Systems - Unholtz-Dickie Corporation
Unholtz-Dickie offers the world’s first all air-cooled, electrodynamic long-stroke testers for telecommunications, earthquake simulation, and transportation applications. Up to 2,300 lbs (1,040 kg) of payload can be supported on a 48x48 inch (1.2 x 1.2 m) footprint on either the slip plate of the horizontal LS12H thruster or the bearing-guided head expander of the vertical LS12V unit. Both are driven by the highly reliable SAI120 SiC amplifier with an integrated switching cabinet for either vertical or horizontal testing. And because it’s an electrodynamic shaker, relatively high frequencies of up to 1,000 Hz can be achieved.

Command Link
-
Unholtz-Dickie Corporation
 Unholtz-Dickie Corporation
The APEX Series Controllers offer an optional RS232 Amplifier/Shaker interface and a software command/status panel to operate UD’s newly enhanced SA and SAI Series amplifier/shaker systems. The SA-Command Link provides identical functionality as the standard SA Amplifier front panel switch buttons, LED status indicators and current/voltage meters. In addition, it provides a Power Save selection to automatically power down the UD SAI Amplifier/Shaker system after a test has finished or aborted, and current / voltage limits can be set to abort the test for added system / specimen protection. Now the complete UD test system can be initiated, monitored, and controlled from one convenient location.

Acquire, Analyze, Import Vibration Data
-
Unholtz-Dickie Corporation
 Unholtz-Dickie Corporation
Reproducing actual field vibration data is a key feature of the APEX Series Vibration Controllers! It provides four distinct and important choices for analyzing and importing data for creation of random, transient shock, and time replication acceleration control (TRAC) tests. Collecting data and importing the information into the controller is accomplished by using the Signal Analyze/Transient Capture and Data Acquisition modes, or by importing stored ASCII file data. The Import Data Manger provides guidance and extensive editing options for optimizing the new test. The resulting test reference (time or frequency spectrum) can then be performed at the vibration test system.

Slip Table Assembly
CSTA Series
-
Unholtz-Dickie Corporation
CSTA Series - Unholtz-Dickie Corporation
Unholtz-Dickie introduced the Combined Slip Table Assembly (CSTA) in the late 1960''s to meet the demand for positive mechanical alignment between the shaker and its companion horizontal slip table. The challenge was to achieve this positive, permanent alignment feature without requiring an expensive seismic mass in the vibration lab floor. The original CSTA design has been continuously improved over the years and has now become the industry standard for permanently aligned, integral reaction mass slip tables.
